children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose more than 2% on Friday, as chipmakers tracked an overnight rally in U.S. peers, but still ended the week lower amid worries about high bond yields.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 178.82 points, or 2.66%, at 6,894.23, marking its biggest daily percentage rise since September 7.
** It logged a 0.2% weekly decline, after rising 3.3% last week.

** "Macroeconomic conditions improved with oil prices falling on easing worries about supply disruptions and U.S. Treasury yields decreasing after the Federal Reserve's policy meeting," said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.

** Wall Street bounced back on Thursday as easing oil prices, dropping US Treasury yields and solid labour data helped markets move beyond the Federal Reserve's first interest rate hike in more than three years. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
rose 3.1%.
** SK Hynix

ended up 6.42%, extending gains after Reuters reported that the chipmaker's subsidiary Solidigm is considering building a NAND flash memory chip factory in the US, with upstate New York emerging as a leading candidate.
** Peer chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 3.37%.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 0.27%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were up 0.55% and 0.83%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.07%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
rose 0.14%.
** Of the total 912 traded issues, 407 shares advanced, while 465 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 424.5 billion won ($306.87 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,383.3 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.13% lower than its previous close at 1,381.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.02 point to 102.23.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 1.5 basis points to 4.043%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 4.1 basis points to 4.471%.
